cells.tense: You are at the table with the pen on what you put into the world.
cells.ask: Offer one finished piece to the next person who can use it. No rework first.
cells.core:
You're starting things and doing it from an even place. Nothing being proved, no performance of enthusiasm — you pick something up because it's worth the pick. A fire gets to burn because it's fed, left alone, and given room to reach its own height.

You're not forcing the timing on any of it. You let a thing take the months it takes and you don't call that slowness. What you're free to feed next is the thinking underneath the doing, the part where what you learned becomes something you can hand to another person. The balance holds because you're not asking the spark to carry more than it can carry.
cells.sheetLine: You're lighting fires from a steady place, and it shows.
cells.verb: Lighting the fire before you know where it will go
cells.place: Where right proportion is being adjusted

cells.tense: You will have settled how it ends before it has even started.
cells.ask: Let one conversation run past where you'd decided it should stop.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of your own fire. It catches, and before it has burned on its own time you've already planned where it lands, who it lands with, what it will mean by the end. You're braced against a future you can't write yet — managing it, steering it, deciding the story before anyone has finished telling it.

Starting well here looks quieter. The direction arrives on its own and you don't have to brace for it. You let the thing burn at its own rate, let the people in the room have their own reactions, and find the shape of it in the doing rather than the forecast. Let the fire reach a place you didn't plan, and the proportion you're forcing after comes back on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You're scripting an ending the fire hasn't reached yet.
cells.verb: Lighting the fire before you know where it will go
cells.place: Where right proportion is being adjusted

cells.tense: You were the one who started things, and you are still at that door.
cells.ask: Put one thing you keep meaning to begin on tomorrow's calendar. Small and real.
cells.core:
A fire that's going well here is fed and tended and left to grow on its own schedule — someone starts something, stays with it, and lets the shine come out of the work itself. Anybody could watch and see it: the thing is picked up, the months are given to it, the whole of it is allowed to take shape.

The fire is burning lower now, and the starting has stopped with it. Don't push yourself into wanting it back. Tend something small and physical instead — learn the actual steps of a craft you keep looking at, give one morning to something with no goal in it. The flame comes back through the hands before it comes back through the head.
cells.sheetLine: You put the fire down and haven't picked it back up.
cells.verb: Lighting the fire before you know where it will go

cells.tense: You are already the one people follow, and you are saying it is the room.
cells.ask: Tell one person out loud that you chose this — name the choice, not the luck.
cells.core:
People pick things up because you picked them up, and that's happening now whether you claim it or not. But when it comes up in conversation the story is that timing did it, the moment was right, the room wanted it. The thing is being run by you and the credit is going somewhere else.

Holding it as yours doesn't mean a louder voice. It means knowing your strength here is what keeps the thing standing, and a builder doesn't have to narrate the build to own it. Say it once, plainly, to one person. What you built doesn't get smaller when you stop calling it luck.
cells.sheetLine: You're already leading. You call it the room doing it.
cells.verb: Lighting the fire before you know where it will go
